title: Add a position-conditioned boundary-pair test with calibrated nulls
statement: For eight specified EVA boundary pairs, the public training pages retain large deviations after right-edge partners are permuted within page, paragraph-first-line status, exact line length and exact boundary index. In ZL, y.q occurs 2,956 times versus 2,219.86 on average under that null and n.q occurs 320 versus 572.86; IT gives 2,960 versus 2,201.28 and 317 versus 593.01. Aggregate discrepancies remain large for both transliterations. These are exploratory findings, not a held-out verdict or a percentage of association attributable to position.
check: Implement a reviewed, prespecified aggregate boundary-pair statistic and a layout-conditioned null. Validate type-I error and power on multiple synthetic books with page, paragraph and position effects, including adjacent boundaries that share a word, sparse strata and exchangeability violations. Prespecify the eight pairs, the standardized discrepancy, grouping, minimum movable samples and the primary null before hidden-page evaluation; reproduce on independent IT. Report actual permutations and all cells, avoid treating percentage change of different null baselines as variance explained.
method: ZL and IT public practice-training pages independently. Paragraph lines only; retain original adjacency and skip pairs with an uncertain token. EVA-basic last glyph of left word and first glyph of right word; chosen pairs y.q, n.q, y.o, n.o, y.ch, n.ch, y.d, n.d. Nulls: randomly permute the right endpoints globally, or within (section, paragraph-first-line indicator, exact line length, zero-based boundary index), or within (page, paragraph-first-line indicator, exact length, exact index). Preserve left endpoints and right endpoint multiset per pool; 199 draws, seed 39086. The aggregate sum of absolute observed-minus-simulation-mean counts divided by square root of simulation mean is exploratory and compared with simulated scores around the same Monte Carlo mean. Paragraph-first-line assignment follows vs.dsl.tokens.
source: Patrick Feaster, Rightward and Downward Grapheme Distributions in the Voynich Manuscript (2022), https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3313/paper12.pdf
limitations: No held-out page identity accessed. 199 permutations yield minimum descriptive tail 0.005. Only 78.2% ZL and 79.1% IT of boundaries are in page-position groups with two or more entries; some of those groups are homogeneous and cannot change. Pool membership ignores whole-word consistency and adjacent boundaries share words; its exchangeability and null calibration are not established. Synthetic checks here are only single independent and linked toy datasets, not a calibrated false-positive study. Since a Monte Carlo centre is estimated from the same replicates, the reported tail is only exploratory. IT is an independent transcription of the same manuscript, not an independent sample of pages.
